hw.name: Hardware joystick robot
hw.goal: A walking, joystick-driven, standing/sitting/holding robot working ON HARDWARE by any means necessary. BC anchors, scripted blends, rot-60 wrappers, specialist checkpoints - all fair game. The KPI is unresolved blockers between the current robot and reliable joystick control, session after session.

arch.name: Advanced architectures
arch.goal: Get a more advanced model (GRU/recurrent/temporal) to walk, stand up, and sit down. Capability research: what architecture learns the full skill set, at what budget, with which failure modes.

nobc.name: Learn without BC anchor
nobc.goal: Learn standing from scratch WITHOUT the help of a BC anchor - and more broadly, honest skill discovery (clean non-scraping gait included) by RL alone: structural rewards, curricula, terrain, RSI. No imitation losses of any kind.

quad.name: Quadruped with two hands
quad.goal: Learn walking on four legs with the two front legs lifted as hands/arms. Stand on four, walk on four, front pair free for tricks.

turn.name: Commanded turning
turn.goal: Make commanded yaw actually work: fix the structural left-yaw drift baked into the walk gait (price tuning doubly closed; mirror-symmetry augmentation is the open lever). De-scoped from the hw deliverable (no camera = no front) but alive as its own research line.

multitask.name: Multitask learning
multitask.goal: Test whether diverse SIMULTANEOUS training beats sequential specialist fine-tuning: a fresh command-conditioned locomotion policy (stand + forward + small yaw/lateral as ONE command family, one coherent reward) vs the specialist path. Decisive A/B/C cohort + transfer test; design doc rl_docs/MULTITASK.md. The campaign's failures look like failure-to-ACQUIRE (narrow gait local optimum), not primarily catastrophic forgetting - this track tests that reframe.

dynrep.name: Dynamics-representation pretraining
dynrep.goal: Learn a task-independent latent of the body's dynamics by self-supervised action-conditioned multi-horizon prediction on diverse sim rollouts (failures included), then test whether PPO reusing that representation (frozen / continually anchored) learns new motor skills with fewer env steps than PPO from scratch. Hard gate: the predictor must beat persistence + linear baselines on held-out data BEFORE any PPO wiring. Design doc rl_docs/DYNREP.md; code rl_move/dynamics/.
